YouTube Product Video

Turn verified product material into a YouTube-native video package while keeping product truth, creative choice, generation consent, media inspection, and publication separate.

Route before acting

  • Use for an organic YouTube long-form video, YouTube Short, YouTube paid ad, shoppable product video, tutorial, explainer, launch, or demonstration.
  • If the user wants only still product images, hand off to Design Room (Ecom).
  • If they want creator-style vertical ads without a specifically YouTube-led deliverable, use UGC Product Ad.
  • If two or more products need a comparison, use Product Buying Guide.
  • If an accepted master already exists and the task is channel adaptation, use Campaign Repurposing.
  • Do not publish externally. Actual channel publication requires a separate explicit request and a real publishing capability.

Required references

Read these before proposing creative directions:

  • Commerce Product Brief
  • Product truth contract
  • Harness interaction contract
  • YouTube method [blocked]

Read these before media generation and delivery respectively:

  • Production workflow [blocked]
  • Delivery and policy [blocked]

Workflow

1. Establish product truth

Inspect the conversation, Canvas, source product images, and any readable sources. Reuse a current Commerce Product Brief when it unambiguously matches the exact product variant. Otherwise run the brief workflow first.

Do not advance a performance claim, price, offer, certification, comparison, personal experience, or product demonstration without the evidence required by the truth contract. A generated lifestyle shot is creative treatment, not proof.

2. Resolve the YouTube route

Infer the route when the user already made it clear. Otherwise use one blocking AskUserQuestion with tailored choices:

  • Organic long-form — a complete explanation, tutorial, launch, or decision aid; default 16:9 unless the user has a reason to differ.
  • YouTube Short — one focused promise with fast visual delivery; default 9:16.
  • Paid YouTube ad — a direct-response or awareness message evaluated with ABCD.

Never ask for a fixed duration before the promise and evidence are understood. Use the shortest duration that fully delivers the selected value. When paid placement, campaign format, or ad inventory imposes a limit, treat that limit as a delivery constraint, not a storytelling formula.

3. Define one viewer promise

Write one sentence that joins:

specific viewer + decision/problem + verified product value + credible payoff

The promise must be strong enough to guide title, thumbnail, opening, script, and CTA. Remove any word the evidence cannot support. Define one primary CTA; secondary information may support it but must not compete with it.

4. Propose two or three tailored directions

Build directions from the actual product, audience, source-image coverage, and route. Do not offer generic templates with only nouns swapped. Each direction must include:

  • viewer promise and title/thumbnail territory;
  • opening image and first spoken or written beat;
  • story spine and proof plan;
  • visual mechanism for turning the supplied stills into honest motion;
  • tone, presenter or no-presenter choice, and audio approach;
  • one real tradeoff or production risk;
  • the primary CTA.

Use AskUserQuestion to select a direction when the choice blocks the script. The chosen direction authorizes continued planning only.

5. Build the script and shot plan

Apply the route-specific method from youtube-method.md.

The plan must connect every shot to a script beat and an evidence role. For each shot specify:

  • purpose and approximate duration;
  • visible subject, action, composition, camera behavior, and transition intent;
  • exact source reference and its authority;
  • voiceover, dialogue, on-screen copy, sound, and caption need;
  • factual claim or creative hypothesis involved;
  • aspect ratio and continuity carrier;
  • whether it is an experiment, standard asset, keyshot, or production clip.

The opening must immediately begin fulfilling the title-and-thumbnail promise. Show the product or its relevant result early enough for the chosen route. Use visible proof before persuasion, include an honest fit or limitation when it affects the purchase decision, and finish with one clear CTA.

For a multi-clip plan, mark the riskiest continuity or product-fidelity unit. Generate that unit first. If it fails, revise the plan before spending on the remaining units.

6. Review the plan before paid work

Present a compact, user-readable script and shot table. Confirm material changes: claims, product variant, presenter identity, core direction, CTA, disclosure treatment, or output route. Do not turn every wording edit into a confirmation round.

Before generation, state the planned output count and that generation may incur charges. Script or shot-plan approval never replaces the platform's generation-cost confirmation.

7. Generate through the current Harness

Follow production-workflow.md exactly:

  1. query the live model contract with tapnow model describe;
  2. choose the method that matches the references and shot intent;
  3. compile model-aware prompts with explicit reference roles;
  4. use tapnow gen +video and its existing confirmation boundary;
  5. submit same-type generations serially unless they form a valid homogeneous batch;
  6. wait for and bind the exact result when completed media is required;
  7. inspect every completed clip with view_media before adopting it;
  8. place accepted clips in Timeline order only when the live client supports --place-in-timeline and --timeline-after.

Never report job_bound, deferred, waiting-for-confirmation, or processing as a completed video. Never rerun the whole workflow after a partial failure; follow returned recovery commands with preserved node and job references.

8. Inspect, revise, and adopt

Review the actual media, not only prompts or job status. Check:

  • exact product identity, label, color, material, proportions, and package;
  • no invented product side, use behavior, result, customer, or endorsement;
  • first-frame clarity and promise delivery;
  • legibility, safe areas, captions, and CTA timing;
  • temporal continuity, hand/object contact, physics, audio, lip sync, and transitions;
  • route-specific quality: appeal/engagement/satisfaction or ABCD;
  • compliance with the approved rights and disclosure plan.

Reject locally weak clips without rewriting approved facts or direction. A new generation still requires the normal generation confirmation behavior.

9. Deliver the YouTube package

Follow delivery-and-policy.md. Name the deliverable honestly:

  • completed master only when a real final exported video exists;
  • Timeline assembly when accepted clips are ordered but not exported;
  • reviewed clip set when individual clips are complete;
  • script and shot plan when no media was generated.

Include accurate packaging, accessibility, disclosure, rights, shopping/tag guidance when applicable, and a controlled analytics-learning plan. Do not guarantee views, retention, virality, sales, or ranking.

Done means

  • the accepted media state is real and inspected;
  • the opening fulfills the same truthful promise made by the title and thumbnail direction;
  • every product claim and comparison remains inside the approved truth brief;
  • the video has one coherent viewer journey and one primary CTA;
  • captions/transcript, disclosures, synthetic-media handling, and rights gaps are visible;
  • the next test changes one declared major variable and names the metric it is meant to teach.
